lesson.title: How classification rules can change
lesson.summary: Track guidance and delegated changes without confusing drafts or proposals with binding amendments.

prerequisites.reason: The learner must distinguish guidance status before reading the classification guidance mandate. The learner must identify the legal provision that a delegated act would change.

blocks: This **extension lesson** explains change mechanisms. It does not gate the core classification path. Article 6(5) provides for Commission classification guidance and examples. Examples help compare facts but are not exhaustive or replacements for the law.
The publication checked on 6 October 2026 remains labelled draft. Always check document identity, status and date again before applying an example to a live decision.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(5)–(8), Article 7, Article 97
Commission draft classification guidance: publication and draft status checked 6 October 2026

blocks: A **delegated act** is a legal mechanism for specified changes under a regulation's authority. Article 6(6) allows adding or modifying paragraph 3 conditions where concrete, reliable evidence shows relevant Annex III systems lack significant harm risk.
A consultation or vendor request is not itself such an amendment. Track the adopted instrument and when it has legal effect.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(5)–(8), Article 7, Article 97
Commission draft classification guidance: publication and draft status checked 6 October 2026

blocks: Article 6(7) requires deleting a derogation condition when concrete, reliable evidence shows that doing so is needed to maintain protection. Paragraph 8 bars decreasing the overall level of protection and requires consistency with the Annex III change mechanism.
Change powers are therefore constrained. The lesson does not predict which conditions will be added or deleted.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(5)–(8), Article 7, Article 97
Commission draft classification guidance: publication and draft status checked 6 October 2026

blocks: Article 7 concerns adding or modifying Annex III use cases in the listed areas using its risk criteria; removal has separate conditions. Keep this distinct from paragraph 3 derogation changes.
A maintainable assessment stores the baseline, monitors actual amendments and rechecks affected facts and rules. Do not freeze a draft example as a permanent statutory exemption.
